en: Krishna said: Again I will tell you the highest knowledge, the best of all knowledge. Knowing it, all the sages have gone from here to the highest perfection.
Those who rely on this knowledge become like me. They are not born even at the creation, nor are they troubled at the end of the world.
Great Brahman (nature) is my womb; I place the seed in it. From that, Bharata, all beings are born.
Kaunteya, whatever forms are born in any womb, great Brahman is their womb and I am the father who gives the seed.
Sattva, rajas and tamas, the three gunas born of nature, bind the undying soul to the body, strong-armed one.
Of these, sattva, being pure, gives light and is free from harm. It binds, sinless one, through attachment to happiness and to knowledge.
Know that rajas is full of passion and comes from craving and attachment. It binds the soul, Kaunteya, through attachment to action.
Know that tamas comes from ignorance and confuses all embodied beings. It binds, Bharata, through carelessness, laziness and sleep.

first: सत्त्वं सुखे संजयति रजः कर्मणि भारत ।
en: Sattva ties one to happiness, rajas to action, Bharata, while tamas covers knowledge and ties one to carelessness.
Sattva rises when it overpowers rajas and tamas, Bharata; rajas rises by overpowering sattva and tamas; and tamas by overpowering sattva and rajas.
When the light of knowledge shines through all the gates of this body, then know that sattva has grown strong.
Greed, busy activity, starting new undertakings, restlessness and longing arise when rajas grows strong, best of the Bharatas.
Darkness, inaction, carelessness and confusion arise when tamas grows strong, joy of the Kurus.

first: यदा सत्त्वे प्रवृद्धे तु प्रलयं याति देहभृत् ।
en: If a person dies when sattva is strong, they reach the pure worlds of those who know the highest.
Dying when rajas is strong, one is born among those attached to action. Dying in tamas, one is born in the wombs of the dull.
The fruit of good action is said to be pure and of the nature of sattva. The fruit of rajas is pain, and the fruit of tamas is ignorance.

first: सत्त्वात्संजायते ज्ञानं रजसो लोभ एव च ।
en: From sattva comes knowledge, from rajas greed, and from tamas come carelessness, confusion and ignorance.

first: ऊर्ध्वं गच्छन्ति सत्त्वस्था मध्ये तिष्ठन्ति राजसाः ।
en: Those in sattva rise upward; those in rajas stay in the middle; those in tamas, living in the lowest guna, sink downward.
When the seer sees no doer other than the gunas, and knows what is beyond the gunas, they come to my state of being.
Going beyond these three gunas, from which the body arises, the soul is freed from birth, death, old age and pain, and gains immortality.
Arjuna said: Lord, by what signs is one known who has gone beyond these three gunas? How do they live, and how do they go beyond the three gunas?

first: प्रकाशं च प्रवृत्तिं च मोहमेव च पाण्डव ।
en: Krishna said: Son of Pandu, such a person does not hate light, activity or confusion when they arise, nor long for them when they stop.
They sit like one who is not involved, not shaken by the gunas. Knowing that it is only the gunas at work, they stay firm and do not waver.

The same in pain and pleasure, resting in the Self, they see a lump of earth, a stone and gold as equal. Steady, they treat the pleasant and the unpleasant alike, and blame and praise of themselves alike.
The same in honour and dishonour, the same to friend and foe, having given up all selfish undertakings: such a person is said to have gone beyond the gunas.
Whoever serves me with unwavering devotion goes beyond these gunas and becomes fit to be one with Brahman.
For I am the ground of Brahman, of the immortal and undying, of eternal right living, and of perfect happiness.
